key_insight: The paper introduces ConfSeq, a conformation description language that lets language models directly work with three-dimensional molecular structures. This bridges text-based AI and molecular geometry, enabling tasks like conformer prediction and 3D molecular generation.
problem_solved: AI models are strong at handling text and sequences, but they often struggle to represent and reason over the complex 3D shapes of molecules. This paper addresses the gap between molecular structure and language-model-based learning.
method: Develops ConfSeq, a language for encoding molecular conformations in a format suitable for language models.
Uses the representation to train or adapt models for 3D molecular tasks such as conformer prediction and molecular generation.
Shows that the approach supports both molecular representation learning and geometry-aware generation with strong performance.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical way to bring foundation-model style methods into 3D chemistry and molecular design. It could simplify building models that understand and generate realistic molecular structures.

paper_title: Bridging three-dimensional molecular structures and artificial intelligence with a conformation description language
paper_authors: Jiacheng Xiong, Yuqi Shi, Min Wu, Panpan Shao, Zhaokun Wang
